$comment: Copy to conf-gen.json and put your real values in it, then run `pnpm gen`.
conf-gen.json is gitignored; this example is the tracked one.
Every option the generator reads is shown below. Required fields are marked
in the $comment of each section; everything else may be omitted, and the
default is given. The first vps/subscription entry is minimal, the second
Any field you add to a vps or subscription entry is also readable from the
loop, so you can carry extra data through without touching the generator.
$comment_output: Where rendered profiles are written. --out overrides it. Default: .conf
$comment_relay: Chained variants are derived from every vps: a second policy named
underlying-proxy in Surge and dialer-proxy in Clash.
$comment_vps: type and params are passed through verbatim, so any protocol both engines
support works — snell, ss, trojan, vmess, hysteria2 and so on. params is
emitted as k=v on the Surge line and as YAML keys in the Clash block;
clashParams is merged over it for keys only Clash understands.
$comment_subscriptions: Required: name, surge, clash.
Optional: prefix, key, filter, surgeFilter, interval, downloadVia,
testUrl, surgeParams, clashOverride.
name       becomes the policy group name in both engines.
surge      policy-path URL for the Surge group.
clash      url for the Clash proxy-provider.
prefix     external-policy-name-prefix in Surge, override.additional-prefix
in Clash. Omit for no prefix.
key        Clash proxy-provider key and cache filename.
Default: the name lowercased with non-alphanumerics removed.
filter     regex selecting which nodes to keep. mihomo searches the name
as the feed sends it, before any prefix is applied. Useful when
a feed carries entries that report quota instead of routing.
surgeFilter  Surge's policy-regex-filter, if it must differ. Surge only
documents "use the policies that the regex matches the policy
name", and in practice an anchored pattern selects nothing
there. So when this is omitted it is derived from filter by
dropping ^ and $ and wrapping in .*, which is correct whether
Surge wants a full match or applies the prefix first. It also
cannot contain a comma, since Surge separates parameters by one.
interval   provider refresh, seconds. Default 3600.
downloadVia  policy used to fetch the subscription. Default DIRECT, so it
does not depend on a working proxy to bootstrap.
testUrl    health-check URL. Default http://cp.cloudflare.com/generate_204.
surgeParams  extra k=v appended to the Surge policy group.
clashOverride  extra keys under the Clash provider's override:.
$comment_vars: Plain {{TOKEN}} substitutions available to every template.
$comment_forbid: Assertions run against the tracked templates, not the rendered output.
These are what make the repository safe to publish: if a real value is ever
typed into a *.base.* file instead of a loop field or token, `pnpm gen`
and `pnpm gen:check` fail before anything is written.
forbidAllow lists literals that are exempt, for addresses that legitimately
appear in a template such as loopback and public resolvers.
